item.title: Paper Awards
item.description:
CP 2025

  • Best Student Paper: Hannes Ihalainen, Jeremias Berg, Matti Järvisalo, and Bart Bogaerts. Symmetric Core Learning for Pseudo-Boolean Optimization by Implicit Hitting Sets

  • Best ML Track Paper: Augustin Parjadis, Quentin Cappart, Bistra Dilkina, Aaron Ferber and Louis-Martin Rousseau. Learning Lagrangian Multipliers for the Travelling Salesman Problem

CP 2001 was the first conference to have paper awards.

item.title: Doctoral Research Award
item.description:
The ACP Doctoral Research Award is awarded every year to a promising young researcher working in the area of constraint programming and who defended their thesis between January and December of the previous two years.

The award, in the form of a certificate, is presented at the CP conference, where the winning researcher will be invited to give a talk about their PhD thesis. The award includes a cash prize of 500 euros, plus free registration for the conference.

item.title: Distinguished Service Award
item.description:
The purpose of this award is to celebrate those CP community members who have made exceptional contributions to support the CP community. Areas of support could include, but are not limited to: association service, service as an editor, conference organisation, representation of CP in other organizations, etc., resulting in positive effects on the research field.

The 2026 call closed on 10 May.

Previous recipients of this award are:

Year Recipient Affiliation
2026 J. Christopher Beck University of Toronto, Canada
2024 Maria Garcia de la Banda Monash University, Australia
2022 Helmut Simonis Insight Centre for Data Analytics, Cork, Ireland
2020 Christian Schulte KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Sweden
2018 Michela Milano University of Bologna, Italy
2016 Thomas Schiex INRA, Toulouse, France
2014 Barry O’Sullivan University College Cork, Ireland
2012 Eugene C. Freuder University College Cork, Ireland
2010 Francesca Rossi University of Padova, Italy

item.title: Early Career Researcher Award
item.description:
The ACP Early Career Researcher Award is awarded every year to a researcher who has completed their PhD at least 2 years and at most 8 years before the year of the competition, with a scientific track record showing great promise in the area of Constraint Programming.

The award was established in 2021 after a proposal by Prof. Eugene Freuder to the ACP. Prof. Freuder has provided seed funding for the award by the donation of the monetary portion of his 2020 IJCAI Research Excellence Award to the ACP.

item.title: Research Excellence Award
item.description: Ten years after the first CP conference, the CP research area was mature enough to begin to identify and honour the most influential people in the field. In 2015, the Executive Committee of the Association for Constraint Programming has decided to establish an annual “ACP award for Research Excellence in constraint programming”, whose purpose is to celebrate those CP researchers who have made exceptional and very influential research contributions to CP with their work.
